about: 50 realistic Indian-law questions. A result counts as a hit when it belongs to `act` and its text contains `anchor` (a phrase from the statute); `section` is the section number it should be. All 50 were checked against the loaded data (Neon): the anchor is present in that Act and under the expected section number; 4 of those sections are flagged possibly_incomplete.
knownGapsInTheData: Code of Civil Procedure, 1908: sections 11 and 20 are not in the data (those numbers hold Order/rule text)
Limitation Act, 1963: only 43 of its sections are present; sections 4, 5 and 7 to 10 are missing
Indian Contract Act, 1872: sections 16, 73 and 124 are missing

questions.question: What is the notice period before filing a cheque bounce complaint?
questions.anchor: receipt of information by him from the bank regarding the return of the cheque as unpaid

questions.question: Within how many days must a cheque bounce complaint be filed after the cause of action arises?
questions.anchor: within one month of the date on which the cause of action arises

questions.question: What is the punishment for dishonour of a cheque for insufficient funds?
questions.anchor: twice the amount of the cheque

questions.question: Is there a legal presumption in favour of the holder of a cheque?
questions.anchor: unless the contrary is proved, that the holder of a cheque received the cheque

questions.question: Who is liable when a company's cheque bounces?
questions.anchor: was in charge of, and was responsible to, the company

questions.question: Can a cheque bounce case be settled by compounding the offence?
questions.anchor: shall be compoundable

questions.question: What is presumed about consideration for a negotiable instrument?
questions.anchor: made or drawn for consideration

questions.question: What makes an agreement a valid contract?
questions.anchor: All agreements are contracts if they are made by the free consent

questions.question: What is free consent in contract law?
questions.anchor: Consent is said to be free when it is not caused by

questions.question: When can a contract be avoided if consent was obtained by coercion or misrepresentation?
questions.anchor: the agreement is a contract voidable at the option of the party whose consent was so caused

questions.question: What counts as fraud that makes a contract voidable?
questions.anchor: Fraud means and includes any of the following acts

questions.question: Who is competent to enter into a contract?
questions.anchor: Every person is competent to contract who is of the age of majority

questions.question: Can a court award reasonable compensation when a contract fixes a penalty for breach?
questions.anchor: reasonable compensation not exceeding the amount so named

questions.question: Is an agreement in restraint of trade valid?
questions.anchor: restrained from exercising a lawful profession, trade or business of any kind, is to that extent void

questions.question: Is an agreement without consideration void?
questions.anchor: An agreement made without consideration is void

questions.question: How far is a surety liable for the debt of the principal debtor?
questions.anchor: liability of the surety is co-extensive with that of the principal debtor

questions.question: What is a contract of guarantee and who is the surety?
questions.anchor: contract of guarantee is a contract to perform the promise

questions.question: What is the punishment for murder?
questions.anchor: Whoever commits murder shall be punished with death or imprisonment for life

questions.question: What is the punishment for theft?
questions.anchor: Whoever commits theft shall be punished

questions.question: What is the offence of cheating and its punishment?
questions.anchor: Whoever, by deceiving any person, fraudulently or dishonestly induces

questions.question: What is criminal breach of trust?
questions.anchor: being in any manner entrusted with property, or with any dominion over property

questions.question: What is the punishment for defamation?
questions.anchor: by words either spoken or intended to be read, or by signs or by visible representations

questions.question: What is dowry death and its punishment?
questions.anchor: death of a woman is caused by any burns or bodily injury

questions.question: Can I get anticipatory bail if I fear arrest?
questions.anchor: reason to believe that he may be arrested on an accusation of having committed a non-bailable offence

questions.question: When can a person accused of a non-bailable offence be released on bail?
questions.anchor: accused of, or suspected of, the commission of any non-bailable offence is arrested or detained without warrant

questions.question: Is the accused entitled to default bail if the police do not file the chargesheet in 60 or 90 days?
questions.anchor: shall be released on bail if he is prepared to and does furnish bail

questions.question: How is an FIR registered for a cognizable offence?
questions.anchor: Every information relating to the commission of a cognizable offence

questions.question: When can a court appoint an arbitrator?
questions.anchor: parties are free to agree on a procedure for appointing the arbitrator

questions.question: Can a court grant interim relief before arbitration starts?
questions.anchor: before or during arbitral proceedings or at any time after the making of the arbitral award

questions.question: On what grounds can an arbitral award be set aside and within what time?
questions.anchor: Recourse to a Court against an arbitral award may be made only by an application for setting aside

questions.question: How is a domestic arbitral award enforced?
questions.anchor: enforced in accordance with the provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure

questions.question: What is an arbitration agreement?
questions.anchor: arbitration agreement means an agreement by the parties to submit to arbitration

questions.question: How does the property of a Hindu male who dies without a will devolve?
questions.anchor: property of a male Hindu dying intestate shall devolve according to the provisions of this Chapter

questions.question: Does an acknowledgment in writing extend the limitation period?
questions.anchor: acknowledgment of liability

questions.question: How is a sale of immovable property defined and completed?
questions.anchor: transfer of ownership in exchange for a price paid or promised

questions.question: What is the difference between a condition and a warranty in a sale of goods?
questions.anchor: stipulation in a contract of sale with reference to goods which are the subject thereof may be a condition or a warranty

questions.question: What is a lease of immovable property?
questions.anchor: transfer of a right to enjoy such property, made for a certain time

questions.question: How is a gift of immovable property made valid?
questions.anchor: transfer must be effected by a registered instrument

questions.question: Where can a consumer file a complaint about defective goods or deficient service?
questions.anchor: may be filed with a District Commission

questions.question: What is a partnership and who is a partner?
questions.anchor: relation between persons who have agreed to share the profits of a business

questions.question: What are the inherent powers of a civil court?
questions.anchor: inherent power of the Court to make such orders as may be necessary for the ends of justice

questions.question: What are the duties of directors of a company?
questions.anchor: director of a company shall act in accordance with the articles of the company

questions.question: Who can apply to the Tribunal for oppression and mismanagement?
questions.anchor: prejudicial to public interest or in a manner prejudicial or oppressive to him or any other member

questions.question: What is the punishment for fraud under company law?
questions.anchor: found to be guilty of fraud

questions.question: What is the punishment for identity theft using a computer?
questions.anchor: fraudulently or dishonestly make use of the electronic signature, password or any other unique identification feature

questions.question: When are online intermediaries exempt from liability for third party content?
questions.anchor: intermediary shall not be liable for any third party information

questions.question: What is the time limit to reply to an RTI application?
questions.anchor: within thirty days of the receipt of the request

questions.question: What is the punishment for drunk driving?
questions.anchor: has, in his blood, alcohol exceeding 30 mg. per 100 ml. of blood

questions.question: Is gratuity payable after five years of service?
questions.anchor: rendered continuous service for not less than five years

questions.question: How can spouses obtain a divorce by mutual consent?
questions.anchor: presented to the district court by both the parties to a marriage together
